changes.policy_area: Admission requirements and EOS procedures for F, J, and I Nonimmigrants
changes.v1_rule: Describing requirements for F and J nonimmigrants seeking admission, including after travel abroad and those approved for OPT and academic training; Updating the cross reference and clarifying the standards for admission in the automatic extension visa validity provisions that cover F and J nonimmigrants applying at a POE after an absence not exceeding 30 days solely in a contiguous territory or adjacent islands; Outlining the process for EOS applications for F, J, and I nonimmigrants; Specifying the effect of departure while an F or J nonimmigrant's application for an EOS in F or J status and/or employment authorization is pending; Providing procedures specific to the transition from D/S to admission for a fixed time period of authorized stay for these nonimmigrants
changes.v2_rule: Describing requirements for F and J nonimmigrants seeking admission, including after travel abroad and those approved for OPT and academic training; Updating cross references and clarifying admission standards for automatic extension visa validity provisions covering F and J nonimmigrants applying at POE after absence not exceeding 30 days solely in contiguous territory or adjacent islands; Outlining EOS application process for F, J, and I nonimmigrants; Providing short-term reprieve for filing EOS during first 6 months after rule takes effect for OPT/STEM OPT; Specifying effect of departure while EOS and/or employment authorization applications are pending; Providing transition procedures from D/S to fixed time period admission; Codifying authorization for F-1 students who timely file EOS to continue full course of study after admission period expiration until EOS adjudicated.
v1_evidence: Describing requirements for F and J nonimmigrants seeking admission, including after travel abroad and those approved for OPT and academic training;

Updating the cross reference and clarifying the standards for admission in the automatic extension visa validity provisions that cover F and J nonimmigrants applying at a port of entry (POE) after an absence not exceeding 30 days solely in a contiguous territory or adjacent islands;
Outlining the process for EOS applications for F, J, and I nonimmigrants;

Specifying the effect of departure while an F or J nonimmigrant's application for an EOS in F or J nonimmigrant status and/or employment authorization (and an associated employment authorization document (EAD)) is pending;
Providing procedures specific to the transition from D/S to admission for a fixed time period of authorized stay for F, J, and I nonimmigrants;
v2_evidence: Describing requirements for F and J nonimmigrants seeking admission, including after travel abroad and those approved for OPT and academic training; Updating the cross reference and clarifying the standards for admission in the automatic extension visa validity provisions that cover F and J nonimmigrants applying at a Port of Entry (POE) after an absence not exceeding 30 days solely in a contiguous territory or adjacent islands; Outlining the process for EOS applications for F, J, and I nonimmigrants; Providing a short-term reprieve from filing for EOS during the first 6 months after the rule takes effect if applying for employment authorization for either post-completion OPT or STEM OPT; Specifying the effect of departure while an F, J, or I nonimmigrant's application for an EOS and/or employment authorization is pending; Providing procedures specific to the transition from D/S to admission for a fixed time period of authorized stay for F, J, and I nonimmigrants; Codifying that an F-1 student who has timely filed an EOS application will be authorized to continue full course of study after admission period expiration until USCIS adjudicates the EOS application.
changes.what_changed: V2 consolidates several V1 provisions into one; adds a short-term 6 month reprieve for filing EOS for OPT/STEM OPT beneficiaries; clarifies that F-1 students with timely filed EOS can continue full course study until EOS adjudication; adds more details on departure effect and transition from D/S to fixed period admission.
changes.practical_effect: Beneficiaries of post-completion OPT/STEM OPT get transitional relief; F-1 students with timely EOS can continue studies pending decision; more detailed rules on admission and EOS process.

changes.v2_rule: Setting the authorized admission and extension periods for F and J nonimmigrants up to the program length, not to exceed a 4-year period

v2_evidence: Setting the authorized admission and extension periods for F and J nonimmigrants up to the program length, not to exceed a 4-year period;

changes.policy_area: First academic year completion requirement before F-1 transfer or change in educational objective
changes.v1_rule: For F-1 students changing educational objectives or transferring to an SEVP-certified school, requiring completion of first academic year at initial school unless SEVP authorizes exception
changes.v2_rule: For F-1 students changing educational objectives or transferring to an SEVP-certified school, requiring completion of first academic year at initial school unless exception authorized by SEVP
v1_evidence: For F-1 students changing educational objectives or transferring to an SEVP-certified school, requiring that the student complete his or her first academic year of a program of study at the school that initially issued his or her Form I-20 or successor form, unless an exception is authorized by SEVP;
v2_evidence: For F-1 students changing educational objectives or transferring to an SEVP-certified school, requiring that the student complete his or her first academic year of a program of study at the school that initially issued his or her Form I-20 or successor form, unless an exception is authorized by SEVP;
changes.what_changed: No material change identified; same requirement and exception retained.

changes.policy_area: Prohibition on graduate-level F-1 students changing programs or transferring without exception
changes.v1_rule: Prohibiting F-1 students at graduate education level from changing programs at any point during study
changes.v2_rule: Prohibiting graduate level F-1 students from changing educational objectives or transferring during study unless exception authorized by SEVP for extenuating circumstances
v1_evidence: Prohibiting F-1 students at the graduate education level from changing programs at any point during a program of study.
v2_evidence: Prohibiting F-1 students at the graduate education level or above from changing educational objectives at any point during a program of study; Prohibiting F-1 students at the graduate education level or above from transferring at any point during their program of study, unless an exception is authorized by SEVP for extenuating circumstances;
changes.what_changed: V2 expands prohibition to include transfers in addition to program changes and allows limited exceptions authorized by SEVP for extenuating circumstances.
changes.practical_effect: Graduate F-1 students have restricted transfer and program change options but may seek SEVP exceptions.

changes.policy_area: Restriction on educational level changes for F-1 nonimmigrants
changes.v1_rule: Requiring new program to be at higher education level than completed program; prohibiting change to same or lower level while in F-1 status
changes.v2_rule: Requiring any nonimmigrant who has completed a program at one educational level to only be allowed to begin another program at a higher educational level and prohibiting change to same or lower level while F-1 student
v1_evidence: Requiring any nonimmigrant who has completed a program at one educational level to only be allowed to begin another program at a higher educational level while in F-1 status and prohibiting a change to the same or a lower educational level while in F-1 status;
v2_evidence: Requiring any nonimmigrant who has completed a program at one educational level to only be allowed to begin another program at a higher educational level as an F-1 student and prohibiting a change to the same or a lower educational level while an F-1 student;
changes.what_changed: No material change identified; requirement to only advance to higher educational level remains consistent.

changes.policy_area: Reduction of allowed departure preparation period for F-1 nonimmigrants
changes.v1_rule: Decreasing allowed period for F-1 nonimmigrants to prepare to depart after completion from 60 to 30 days
changes.v2_rule: Decreasing allowed period to 30 days; adding requirement to depart or maintain lawful status within 30 days if study or training ends early
v1_evidence: Decreasing from 60 to 30 days the allowed period for F-1 nonimmigrants to prepare to depart from the United States after completion of a course of study or authorized period of post-completion practical training;
v2_evidence: Decreasing the period allowed for F-1 nonimmigrants to prepare to depart from the United States after completion of a course of study or an authorized period of post-completion practical training from 60 to 30 days; Requiring that if an F-1 student ends study or training early, the student and eligible dependents must depart the U.S. or take action to maintain lawful status within 30 days of the end date;
changes.what_changed: V2 adds explicit obligation to depart or maintain lawful status within 30 days if study or training ends early, beyond reduction from 60 to 30 days.
changes.practical_effect: F-1 students ending studies earlier than programmed must depart or act to maintain status within 30 days, enhancing compliance enforcement.

changes.policy_area: Unacceptable reasons for F program extensions
changes.v1_rule: Delays caused by academic probation, suspension, or student's repeated inability or unwillingness to complete course are unacceptable reasons for program extensions for F nonimmigrants
changes.v2_rule: Delays caused by academic probation, suspension, or student's repeated inability or unwillingness to complete course of study is generally unacceptable reason for program extensions for F nonimmigrants
v1_evidence: Providing that a delay in completing one's program by the program end date specified on the Form I-20, which includes but is not limited to delays caused by academic probation or suspension or a student's repeated inability or unwillingness to complete his or her course of study, generally is an unacceptable reason for program extensions for F nonimmigrants;
v2_evidence: Providing that a delay in completing one's program by the program end date specified on the Form I-20, which includes but is not limited to delays caused by academic probation or suspension or a student's repeated inability or unwillingness to complete his or her course of study, is generally an unacceptable reason for program extensions for F nonimmigrants;
changes.what_changed: No substantive change; provisions are consistent on unacceptable reasons for program extensions.

changes.policy_area: Auto-extension of employment authorization for F nonimmigrants with pending EOS due to severe economic hardship
changes.v1_rule: Allowing F nonimmigrants with timely filed EOS applications pending after admission period expiration to receive auto-extension of employment authorization up to 240 days or Federal Register notice end date due to severe economic hardship from emergent circumstances
changes.v2_rule: Allowing F nonimmigrants with timely filed EOS applications pending after admission period expiration to receive auto-extension of employment authorization up to 240 days or Federal Register notice end date due to severe economic hardship from emergent circumstances
v1_evidence: Allowing F nonimmigrants whose timely filed EOS applications remain pending after their admission period has expired to receive an auto-extension of their current authorization for on-campus and off-campus employment based on severe economic hardship resulting from emergent circumstances under existing 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(v). The length of the auto-extension of employment authorization would be up to 240 days or the end date of the Federal Register notice announcing the suspension of certain regulatory requirements, whichever is earlier;
v2_evidence: Allowing F nonimmigrants whose timely filed EOS applications remain pending after their admission period has expired to receive an auto-extension of their current authorization for on-campus and off-campus employment based on severe economic hardship resulting from emergent circumstances under existing 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(v). The length of the auto-extension of employment authorization will be up to 240 days or the end date of the Federal Register notice announcing the suspension of certain regulatory requirements, whichever is earlier;
changes.what_changed: No material change identified; auto-extension provisions with same conditions and limits.

changes.policy_area: Replacement of D/S with fixed time period admission for I nonimmigrants with exceptions for PRC nationals
changes.v1_rule: Replacing D/S for I nonimmigrants with admission for fixed time period not exceeding 240 days (except some PRC nationals), with EOS available for those meeting requirements
changes.v2_rule: Replacing D/S for I nonimmigrants with admission for fixed time period until activities completed, not to exceed 240 days (except some PRC nationals), with EOS available for those meeting requirements
v1_evidence: Replacing D/S for I nonimmigrants with admission for a fixed time period until they complete the activities or assignments consistent with the I classification, not to exceed 240 days (with the exception of some I aliens from the People's Republic of China), with an EOS available for I nonimmigrants who can meet specified EOS requirements;
v2_evidence: Replacing D/S for I nonimmigrants with admission for a fixed time period until they complete the activities or assignments consistent with the I classification, not to exceed 240 days (with the exception of some I nonimmigrants from PRC), with an EOS available for those meeting requirements;
changes.what_changed: V2 clarifies admission lasts until activities or assignments completed and explicitly excludes certain PRC nationals from 240-day max except for exceptions; similar EOS availability provision.
changes.practical_effect: I nonimmigrants, including some PRC nationals, have limited fixed admission period with possibility of EOS.

changes.policy_area: Continued employment authorization for J-1 and I nonimmigrants with pending EOS
changes.v1_rule: J-1 nonimmigrants employment authorized with specific employer incident to status continue up to 240 days if EOS pending; J-2 dependents lose authorization after EAD expires; I nonimmigrants authorized to continue working up to 240 days (90 days for some PRC passport holders) while EOS pending
changes.v2_rule: J-1 nonimmigrants employment authorized with specific employer incident to status continue for up to 240 days if EOS pending; J-2 dependents lose authorization after EAD expires; I nonimmigrants authorized to continue working for up to 240 days (90 days for PRC nationals) while EOS pending
v1_evidence: Clarifying that J-1 nonimmigrants who are employment authorized with a specific employer incident to status, continue to be authorized for such employment for up to 240 days under 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20) if status expires while their timely filed EOS application is pending, whereas J-2 dependents, who must apply for employment authorization as evidenced by an EAD, do not have the benefit of continued work authorization once the EAD expires;

Clarifying that I nonimmigrants are authorized to continue working in the United States for their foreign employer, under 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20), while their timely filed EOS application is pending for up to 240 days; \22\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
\22\ This time period is limited to up to 90 days for I nonimmigrants with a passport from the People's Republic of China but does not include those with a Hong Kong Special Administrative Region passport or a Macau Special Administrative Region passport.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
v2_evidence: Clarifying that J-1 nonimmigrants who are employment authorized with a specific employer incident to status continue to be authorized for such employment for up to 240 days under the existing regulatory provision at 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20) if their status expires while their timely filed EOS application is pending, whereas J-2 dependents, who must apply for employment authorization as evidenced by an EAD, do not have the benefit of continued work authorization once the EAD expires;

Clarifying that I nonimmigrants are authorized to continue working in the United States for their foreign employer, under 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20), for up to 240 days (with the exception of I nonimmigrants from the PRC who may continue working for up to 90 days) while their timely filed EOS application is pending;
changes.what_changed: No material change; V2 clarifies same conditions and time limits for J-1 and I nonimmigrants' continued employment authorization pending EOS.
